title: protect workflow rate-limit logging: read x-ratelimit-remaining from the latest real REST response via an Octokit hook, not from GET /rate_limit
answers: Why does the protect workflow log a rate limit remaining number that never changes?
How do I log another GitHub API header or counter in the CI check-polling script?
Where is the 'Rate limit remaining' message printed for the protection workflow?
Why did we stop calling the rate_limit endpoint in the protect workflow?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/protect.js:module.exports is the GitHub Actions script that polls the PR's check runs until they finish (fetchChecks, the sleep/polling loop, and the pending-jobs count). Every REST call it makes goes through the Octokit `github` client passed in by actions/github-script.
Rule: Register `github.hook.after("request", ...)` once at the top of module.exports and store `response.headers["x-ratelimit-remaining"]` in a closure variable; log that stored value once per polling iteration after fetchChecks. Do not issue a standalone GET /rate_limit call to report quota, since the PR notes that endpoint returned a fixed 15,000 allowance rather than the quota consumed by the script's own requests.
Constraints: The logged value is the header from the most recent real API response, so it is undefined until the first request completes; the loop guards with `if (rateLimitRemaining !== undefined)`. Other headers can be captured the same way in the hook. This applies only to the protect.js polling script, not to other workflows.
applies: GitHub Actions protect.js check-polling script in .github/workflows; applies to any change to how it reports GitHub REST quota.
says: The remaining API quota count in pull request check logs never changes.
Pull request protection workflow logs always show a static rate limit allowance.
Display the actual remaining GitHub request quota in the branch protection log output.
Check status polling logs report a frozen rate limit counter during pull requests.
search: In .github/workflows/protect.js, rate-limit remaining logging must capture response.headers["x-ratelimit-remaining"] via an Octokit github.hook.after("request", ...) hook registered in module.exports and log it once per polling iteration after fetchChecks. Standalone GET /rate_limit calls must not be used because that endpoint returns a fixed 15,000 allowance rather than quota consumed by the script. The logged value is undefined until the first request completes and is guarded by checking rateLimitRemaining !== undefined; this rule applies only to the protect.js polling script in .github/workflows.
